summary: Point Judith Light has marked the west side of Narragansett Bay's entrance since 1810; its 1857 tower stands beside an active Coast Guard station, closed to visitors.

fog_signal.note: Brick fog signal building of 1923; horn sounds one blast every fifteen seconds (nomination)

access.note: Beside the Point Judith Coast Guard Station, on a lot the station shares (NRHP). Grounds and tower closed to visitors (LighthouseFriends, as of 2013; a visitor guide says the same). The archive record says open to the public.

corrections.why: The record's stone tower of 1810 is the first tower, which was wooden and was destroyed in 1815. The 1816 stone tower was replaced in 1857, and the present tower dates from 1857 (nomination; archive record tower established 1857).

The nomination says 'Accessible - yes, restricted'. LighthouseFriends says the lighthouse is owned by the Coast Guard, grounds and tower closed, and the grounds no longer accessible as of 2013. A visitor guide says the grounds are no longer open. The archive record says open to the public.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1810 tower is the first, wooden tower; the nomination says it was destroyed in 1815. The 1816 stone tower was replaced in 1857 by the present tower. The present tower is the 1857 one.
The nomination and LighthouseFriends give a range of 16 miles, as printed. The archive record gives no range. The story uses miles because no source says nautical miles.

notes_for_editor: (1) Keepers: roster.py, USLHS place 3500, 42 lines, matched by name and position (0.07 km). Names and spans are the archive's, from NARA registers via Kraig Anderson's inventory; none was checked against a primary register. The story says the nineteen principal-keeper entries run from Whitford (1809-1835) and that Robert A. Bauer's entry is open-ended (from 1961); the archive lists Donald F. Barrows (1961) after Bauer in its own order. (2) Post-1954 entries: the nomination says the light was automated in 1954 and then maintained by Coast Guard station personnel; the archive roster and LighthouseFriends list keepers to 1961 (Robert A. Bauer from 1961). The story reports both; the sources do not reconcile them. (3) Assistant for the fog signal: the nomination says one was hired in 1874; LighthouseFriends says one was hired when the first fog signal went in, in 1867; the roster lists assistants from 1867. Not reconciled. (4) Tower material and height: the nomination says granite blocks, 51 ft tower, light 65 ft above sea level; the archive says brownstone, 65 ft light above water, and 46 ft from base to lantern center; LighthouseFriends says brownstone and a tower rising 65 ft above the water. The story gives the nomination's 51 ft (15.5 m) and the archive's 46 ft (14 m) and states the disagreement. (5) Oil house: the 1916 Commissioner's report describes a concrete oil house under construction at the close of fiscal 1916; the nomination says brick, built 1917. Not reconciled. (6) The 1899 Board line (color of tower changed 15 May 1899) is in the general list of color changes in existing lights (scan page 24), not a Third District list; the printed page was not read. (7) LighthouseFriends is secondary and copyrighted: facts only, paraphrased, with short quotations for evidence. Its wreck list is not checked against primary sources. (8) Narragansett Herald, 17 Aug 1889, p. 5: the sentence reads 'Joseph Whaley, for over 27 years in charge of the lighthouse at Point Judith, has resigned, and his son, Henry A. Whaley, %ms been appointed in his place.' The OCR's '%ms' is read as 'has'; the story relies on the OCR for 'had been appointed' and cites the Herald only for the resignation and succession. The Herald's OCR was not checked against the page image. (9) Access: the brief says public; the archive says open; the nomination says 'Accessible - yes, restricted'; LighthouseFriends and a visitor guide say closed. Check on the ground or with the Coast Guard before any visit. (10) The Point Judith Life-Saving Station (1876, about 50 yards east, per the nomination) is a separate station record and is mentioned only in passing. Its wrecks are not in this story. (11) The archive's 'Other Structures' line gives a radiobeacon building of 1939; the nomination gives 1931 for the radio beacon house. Not used in the story. (12) Range: the nomination and LighthouseFriends give 16 miles as printed. The station record's range_nm key was removed because no source states nautical miles. (13) Photos: none proposed; the USCG photographs credited in LighthouseFriends are not verified for licence. (14) Page images checked for this story: the 1938 Bulletin PDF page 40 (printed page 136) reads 'In Rhode Island, serious damage was experienced at a number of stations, including ... Point Judith'; the Bulletin's Tulip article reads 'the recent hurricane which struck the New England coast'. (15) Fact-check 2026-10-22: quotes re-checked (84 found on the first run); story sentences checked against the NRHP nomination pages, the USLHS place record, LighthouseFriends, the nelights visitor guide, the 1895 and 1899 Light-House Board reports, the FY1916 Commissioner report (scan p. 161, printed p. 52, confirmed by the archive's scan data) and the 1938 Bulletin.
